topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and sets out the key learning outcomes regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Conventional Cancer Therapies: Surgery, Radiotherapy, and Cytotoxic Chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary conventional modalities used to physically debulk or cytotoxically kill cancer cells, along with their clinical limitations and toxicity.

topics.label: Exploiting Intrinsic Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities and Checkpoint Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss strategies that take advantage of specific tumor vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependence, defective cell cycle checkpoints, and impaired DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase Inhibitors, Oncogene Addiction, and Resistance Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine targeted therapy against hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the mechanisms, such as gatekeeper mutations and bypass signaling, through which tumor cells develop drug resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-Based Targeted Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how engineered monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates target specific cell-surface proteins to eliminate cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer Immunology and Cellular Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relationship between the immune system and cancer, detailing modern immunotherapies including checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific antibodies, and CAR-T cells.

topics.label: Systemic Challenges, Historical Trends, and Future Directions in Cancer Treatment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics assess the broader clinical challenges, long-term survival trends, ethical dilemmas, and future opportunities in cancer medicine.
